absent: Vendor-specific CR0 and CR4 validity, get and set hook behavior and reserved-bit computation.
MMU context reset, unload, new base, root reclamation, role-bit definitions and internal locking.
Legal directory-base checks, PAE pointer load, translation-enable flag and paging-mode helper internals.
EFER validation and set behavior and code-segment width query internals.
In-kernel LAPIC presence, priority set and get, APIC-base update and fault-address handling.
Queued-exception creation, injection, capability enablement and general exception flow beyond save selection and delivery.
General-register save and restore, instruction-pointer, processor-mode, bootstrap and halt-state helper internals.
VCPU load and put, SRCU scope rules, register cache and dirty tracking, and sleep constraints beyond observed pairing.
Confidential-guest post-CR3 path and protected-state lifecycle beyond observed early returns.
Exact numeric values and bit positions of control, debug, request and userspace-interface constants.

findings.text: CR0 management interface defines acceptance conditions for candidate values and the MMU and TLB maintenance associated with successful updates, including a narrow low-bit update path.
CR3 and PCID invalidation interface defines acceptance conditions for page-directory base updates and the TLB and shadow-root consequences of accepted values.
CR4 management interface defines acceptance conditions for candidate values and the MMU and TLB maintenance associated with successful updates.
Priority and segment accessors expose task priority and segment state, using in-kernel LAPIC handling when present and vendor segment hooks for segment images.
Special-register save and restore interface defines which segments, descriptor tables, control registers, EFER, APIC base, interrupt indication and optional PAE pointers are visible to userspace.
Run-time shared-area propagation and breakpoint-register interfaces define exchange between shared run area and vCPU state and validity conditions for debug-register updates.
Exception-payload handling defines selection of the migratable queued exception and the architectural effects of payload delivery, including compatibility behavior on state save.
A CR0 candidate is refused when upper half is set on 64-bit hosts, when not-write-through without cache disable holds, when paging without protection enable holds, or when vendor validity fails.

Accepted CR0 updates satisfy compatibility among forced extension-type, cleared reserved positions, long-mode entry requirements on PAE and code width, pointer-load success on relevant toggles, and prohibitions involving 64-bit mode, PCID use and CET without write protect.

Post-update consequences of CR0 include distinct handling for write-protect-only changes under paging and translated paging, guest TLB flush on paging disable, async-fault readiness on paging enable where enabled, and MMU context reset on role-bit divergence.
Narrow machine-status-word update affects only the low control bits and is subject to the normal CR0 acceptance path while other bits are preserved.
Accepted CR3 updates satisfy legality and PAE-pointer requirements, with PCID and no-flush controls determining flush suppression and with equal-value non-PAE stores needing only flush consideration.
PAE paging holds exactly when paging and PAE are enabled outside long mode.

PCID invalidation consequences include guest TLB flush under translated paging, MMU sync plus current flush for matching active identifier, early completion when PCID use is disabled, and reclamation of prior roots carrying the target identifier when enabled.

CR4 candidates intersecting guest-reserved positions or rejected by vendor validity are refused; accepted long-mode values require PAE and stable wide-addressing selection, accepted paging values require pointer-load success on relevant toggles, PCID enable requires zero low directory base and long mode, and CET requires write protect.

Post-update consequences of CR4 include MMU context reset on role-bit divergence, MMU unload on disabled-to-enabled PCID without translation, guest-wide flush on global-page or enabled-to-disabled PCID changes, and current-context flush on PAE toggle or supervisor-execution-enable.

Priority updates with reserved positions set are refused; otherwise priority is held by in-kernel LAPIC when present and by stored vCPU field otherwise, while queued-interrupt state comprises present indication, software indication and vector.

Protected guests expose only a subset of special registers on save; unprotected saves additionally include segments, descriptor tables and fault registers, plus a single outgoing interrupt-bit for hard injected interrupts, with pending-exception compatibility delivery applied first.

The migratable exception is the VM-exit record only when it alone is pending without a pending or injected regular exception; debug payload folds into status with fixed-bit handling and a cleared reserved position, fault payload becomes fault address, and delivery clears stored payload.
When exception-payload capability is off, any pending payload on the migratable exception is delivered into architectural state at save time.

Combined special-register images with long-mode enable plus paging require PAE, active long mode and legal directory base, while other images forbid active long mode and 64-bit code; images also require individually valid CR4, CR0 and EFER.

Successful restore is characterized by descriptor tables, control state, segments and priority reflecting the image, MMU-reset indication on control divergence or PAE-pointer activity, and runnable state for a specific reset-vector bootstrap processor.
Restore consequences include MMU reset plus guest-wide flush when indicated and a pending hard interrupt derived from the lowest set position in the incoming bitmap.

Extended save reports up to four directory pointers as valid only under PAE paging; extended restore rejects unknown flags and userspace pointers outside PAE paging or for protected guests, otherwise installs supplied pointers, marks them dirty and from userspace, and indicates MMU reset.

Shared-area propagation is gated by valid and dirty masks for general and special registers, clearing dirty indication only after successful application and failing the whole update on invalid special-register image.

Breakpoint address registers update stored and effective copies, with effective update suppressed under hardware-breakpoint debugging; status and control aliases enforce validity, preserve fixed positions with capability-dependent additions, and refresh derived control state.
Directory-pointer reads may sleep and refresh from vendor cache when unavailable; writes store the slot value with dirty tracking handled by the caller.
Architectural save and restore hold the vCPU loaded across the operation; PAE-pointer save holds vCPU SRCU read side while copying entries and restore holds SRCU while reloading.

Observed architectural state comprises control and debug registers, EFER and APIC base, segment and descriptor-table images, a queued-interrupt triple and two queued-exception records with payload flags, four directory-pointer slots with userspace-origin indication, and MMU current plus prior roots.
Paging-mode relationships among non-paging, PAE paging and long mode constrain control and EFER combinations and select TLB scope among none, current context and guest-wide plus MMU reset or unload.

Queued exception and interrupt state spans empty, pending with optional payload, injected, and delivered into architectural state, with save-time compatibility delivery and single-bit migration of hard interrupts.

Userspace entry points for special-register management comprise legacy get and set operations that reject protected state, plus extended get and set variants and shared-area sync helpers gated by capability masks.

Wrong TLB scope or missed MMU maintenance on control toggles can leave stale translations or reusable prior roots; PCID enable without root reclamation risks later no-flush reuse, and pointer-load failure must veto the update.

Debug and exception hazards include leaking pending payload across save-restore when capability is off, losing breakpoint intent under guest debugging, and restoring more than one pending interrupt from the bitmap.

Observed control ABI names include CR0 paging, protection, cache, write-protect and extension-type positions plus reserved and role-bit sets, CR4 PAE, global-page, PCID, execution-protection, wide-address and CET positions plus reserved and role-bit sets, CR3 PCID mask and no-flush, CR8 reserved set, and EFER long-mode enable and active positions.

Observed KVM ABI names include guest TLB flush, current flush, MMU sync, async-fault ready and event requests, sync-register general and special masks, extended-register pointer-valid flag, segment and register selectors, interrupt count, debug vectors and fixed or volatile masks, guest-debug breakpoint use, and runnable processor state.
